title: Abraham and Melchizedek
credit_line: Gift of the Provident Securities Company
identifying_description: Scene illustrating the story of Abraham and Melchizedek from the Book of Genesis.
web_text: Old EDEC Label Text:Abraham and MelchizedekFranco-Flemish, probably Tournai, 1460-1470Wool, silk; tapestry weaveGift of the Provident Securities Co. 1969.15This story from the Book of Genesis tells the meeting of Abraham and Melchizedek after the battle of Dan. Melchizedek, the priest-king of Salem, brings bread and wine to the patriarch and blesses him. Abraham offers Melchizedek one tenth of his plunder. The tapestry is divided compositionally along the diagonal line-the battle in progress is shown at the left and the meeting of the two men at the right. Abraham, with his flowing beard, gently bends his armored knee as he takes the bread and wine from Melchizedek, adorned in elaborate robes and a bejeweled crown. The high horizon, flattening of forms, and extreme chaos of the battle scene are typical of the Tournai tapestries of the time.
